stories.text: Chancellor Healey's first Budget offers 100 pounds toward energy bills and a tax on banks, but opposition parties call it too timid.
Spain starts three days of mourning after a train crash killed dozens, one of the worst European rail disasters in modern times.
Partial results from the Israeli election, with 85 percent counted, give Netanyahu's Likud and allies 53 of 120 Knesset seats, short of a majority.
Defeated Brazilian candidate Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Miami and denies fleeing, repeating unproven claims of a coup and electoral fraud against him.
Police close their inquiry after the August death of Heroes and Nashville actress Hayden Panettiere, from fentanyl, Xanax and other drugs, is ruled accidental.
Items linked to George Michael, including his Faith guitar, are going to auction, but the brother of his late assistant says she would have objected.
On the second day of his Caribbean tour, King Charles honours fallen service members on the island and later shows off his dancing.
Hackers calling themselves the Department of Peace publish details of over 41,000 DHS employees, including thousands of US immigration agents.
A construction surge in parts of Nepal and India's Uttarakhand has put 300,000 people at risk from potential Himalayan disasters.
Recycling industry leaders warn that used needles are turning up more often in household waste as weight-loss injections grow in popularity.
